headline: High: Copilot can write and modify repo state while the paired content source has broad network egress, creating default-path leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing source with no documented shared channel to B, while B ingests editor buffers and repo context and can propose edits. The pairwise injection path is therefore indirect and not proven by the profiles; uncertainty keeps this above none, but below medium because no shared filesystem or MCP bridge is shown.
conditions: IF A's output is copied into B's editor buffers or repo context, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF B is configured to treat pasted text as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting A output into B without review.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from A output.
Disable automatic ingestion of external text into B where possible.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has broad network egress, and B reads editor buffers and repo context plus calls api.githubcopilot.com. Even though A touches no explicit sensitive class and the shared data path is not fully documented, B can transmit context off-host by default, so leakage of whatever A contributes is plausible in normal use.
conditions: IF A is given secrets, source code, or regulated text, B may relay that context to its backend.
IF B is used on a repository containing sensitive files, those contents can enter the model context.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared repo context.
Use a redacted workspace for B.
Restrict B to non-sensitive repositories.
Review Copilot privacy and retention settings before use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress, while B can write_filesystem and modify_git_state in editor-scoped sessions. That creates overlapping influence over mutable project state and external resources; the profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflict is plausible in default workflows even though A itself is not runnable.
conditions: IF A's recommendations are applied into the same repo that B edits, concurrent changes can collide.
IF multiple B instances edit the same repository, git-state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign one agent per branch.
Require human review before applying B edits.
Use short-lived feature branches.
Pause A-driven changes while B is editing the same files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing source and B is a coding assistant that can propose edits to repo context. If B treats A's generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or documentation changes; the profiles show no built-in verification step, so the pathway exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated instructions or facts without verification, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF A produces incorrect code guidance, B may incorporate it into edits.
mitigations: Require source verification before applying A output.
Use B only after a human review of A's claims.
Add a checklist for factual claims in A output.
Keep A output out of auto-applied edit flows.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source docs-only with no touched data classes, while B is a closed-source coding assistant that handles repo context and sends it to api.githubcopilot.com. The main compliance concern is policy mismatch around code and workspace data, but the profiles do not show a residency or regulated-data violation, so this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in B's repo context, compliance obligations may apply.
IF organizational policy forbids sending code context to third-party APIs, B may violate it.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B contexts.
Confirm vendor policy and DPA before use.
Use a non-sensitive test repository.
Document retention and access rules for the workspace.
